Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1011
Claimant:
Chad Richmond
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
2025-05-21
Claimant reported a sideswipe that occurred while changing lanes on a multi-lane road, with the other vehicle moving
into the claimant's lane and making contact along the passenger side. The claimant is unrepresented and provided an
initial statement by phone, describing neck and back pain beginning shortly after the impact.
2025-06-21
Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant and the damage pattern on the vehicle, which lines up with the
described impact along the side panels and mirror. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file
suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The driver is shown as a named driver on the policy.
2025-07-20
Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the lane change and the contact between the two vehicles. Two
independent witnesses in nearby vehicles gave statements that macth the claimant's account of how the collision
happened.
2025-09-16
Medical records show the claimant was seen for neck and back strain, with the type and level of injury fitting the force
of a side impact. No prior injury to the same body areas is on record. Treatment followed a typical course and eased
off as the claimant improved.
2025-10-25
The cliamant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far. It is not yet fully clear from the
statements and photos exactly where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at the moment of impact, so I have
requested a follow-up question on seating position.
2025-11-27
Based on the photos, witness statements, the other driver's confirmation, and the medical picture, the claim is
consistent across sources and I am recommending it proceed to standard settlement review, with the seating position
question noted as the only open item.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
